questions.stem: Which subatomic particle has a negligible mass and a negative charge?
questions.explanation: An electron carries a relative charge of -1 and has a mass of about 1/1836 of a proton, which is treated as negligible. This is why the mass of an atom is taken as the sum of its protons and neutrons only.

distractorRationale.a: A proton has relative mass 1 and a positive charge
distractorRationale.b: A neutron has relative mass 1 and no charge
distractorRationale.d: Nucleon is the collective name for protons and neutrons, both of which have relative mass 1

questions.stem: An atom of aluminium has atomic number 13 and mass number 27. How many neutrons does it contain?
questions.explanation: The mass number counts protons plus neutrons, so neutrons = mass number minus atomic number = 27 - 13 = 14. The atomic number 13 gives the proton count, which for a neutral atom also equals the electron count.

distractorRationale.a: 13 is the number of protons, not neutrons
distractorRationale.c: 27 is the total number of nucleons, protons and neutrons together
distractorRationale.d: 40 comes from adding 27 and 13 instead of subtracting

questions.stem: A sulphide ion, S2-, is formed from an atom with atomic number 16 and mass number 32. The numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons in the ion are respectively
questions.explanation: Ion formation only involves electrons. The nucleus keeps its 16 protons and its 32 - 16 = 16 neutrons. A 2- charge means two extra electrons have been gained, so the electron count rises from 16 to 18.

distractorRationale.a: This is the neutral sulphur atom; it ignores the two electrons gained
distractorRationale.c: Protons were increased to match the electron count, but the nucleus is unchanged when an ion forms
distractorRationale.d: The extra two particles were added to the neutrons rather than the electrons

questions.stem: Boron exists as two isotopes: boron-10 with 20 percent abundance and boron-11 with 80 percent abundance. Its relative atomic mass is
questions.explanation: Take the weighted average: [(10 x 20) + (11 x 80)] / 100 = (200 + 880) / 100 = 1080 / 100 = 10.8. The answer sits closer to 11 than to 10 because boron-11 is far more abundant, which is a useful check.

distractorRationale.a: The abundances were swapped, weighting boron-10 too heavily
distractorRationale.b: A simple average of 10 and 11 was taken, ignoring the abundances
distractorRationale.d: The two isotopic masses were added instead of averaged

questions.stem: Isotopes of an element have identical chemical properties because they have the same
questions.explanation: Chemical reactions involve only the outermost electrons. Isotopes have the same atomic number, so they have the same number of electrons arranged in the same way, and therefore they react identically. Their differing neutron numbers affect mass-dependent physical properties only.

distractorRationale.a: Differing neutron numbers are precisely what makes them isotopes in the first place
distractorRationale.b: Isotopes have different mass numbers
distractorRationale.d: Density depends on mass, so isotopes actually differ slightly in density

questions.stem: Copper has two isotopes: copper-63 with an abundance of 69.2 percent and copper-65 with an abundance of 30.8 percent. Calculate the relative atomic mass of copper to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: The weighted average is [(63 x 69.2) + (65 x 30.8)] / 100. That gives (4359.6 + 2002.0) / 100 = 6361.6 / 100 = 63.616, which rounds to 63.6. The value lies between 63 and 65 and leans towards 63 because copper-63 is more than twice as abundant.

questions.stem: Species X has 12 protons and 10 electrons. Species Y has 8 protons and 10 electrons. Which statement is correct?

options.text: X and Y are isotopes of the same element
X is a 2+ cation and Y is a 2- anion, and both are isoelectronic
X and Y are both neutral atoms
X is an anion and Y is a cation

questions.explanation: X has two more protons than electrons, giving a 2+ charge, so it is the magnesium ion Mg2+. Y has two more electrons than protons, giving a 2- charge, so it is the oxide ion O2-. Both have 10 electrons, so they are isoelectronic with neon.

distractorRationale.a: Isotopes must have the same proton number; 12 and 8 are different elements
distractorRationale.c: A neutral atom has equal protons and electrons, which is not the case for either species
distractorRationale.d: The charges are reversed: an excess of protons gives a cation, an excess of electrons gives an anion

distractorRationale.b: Electrons have a negative charge, not protons.
distractorRationale.c: Neutrons are neutral particles and do not carry any charge.
distractorRationale.d: Protons have a fixed positive charge and do not vary.
